result.note: Tested the Manila meeting venue, FY2025/26 India–China trade figures and the timeline of the thaw; skipped the planned 1 August border trade restart as a forward-looking plan.

questions.prompt: In July 2026, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting held in which city?
questions.explain: The two ministers met in Manila on 22 July 2026 on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting. Jaishankar raised fair market access, supply-chain predictability and the trade imbalance.
questions.source: The two met in Manila on the sidelines of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Meeting on Wednesday.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's trade with China in fiscal year 2025/26:
items: India's imports from China reached USD 132 billion, its highest from any nation.
Total India–China trade stood at USD 151.10 billion.
India's trade deficit with China was below USD 50 billion.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong: the deficit was above USD 100 billion. Jaishankar pressed Wang Yi on this lopsided balance as New Delhi seeks to make the thaw pay off in trade terms.
questions.source: India's imports from China still hit USD 132 billion in fiscal year 2025/26, its highest from any nation, leaving a deficit above USD 100 billion within total trade of USD 151.10 billion.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the recovery in India–China relations as described in July 2026:
items: Ties began recovering after Prime Minister Modi met President Xi in October 2024.
The friction that preceded the recovery dated to the 2020 border clash.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Both are correct: the Modi–Xi meeting of October 2024 ended friction dating to the 2020 border clash. Since then direct flights have resumed and business visas for Chinese professionals have been eased.
questions.source: Ties began recovering after Modi met President Xi in October 2024, ending friction that dated to the 2020 border clash.
